facts.statement: The species was originally classified under the names Megalosaurus meriani, Cetiosauriscus greppini, and Ornithopsis greppini before being moved to the genus Amanzia.
facts.quote: synonyms: *Megalosaurus meriani (in part) Greppin, 1870 Cetiosauriscus greppini (von Huene, 1922) Ornithopsis greppini von Huene, 1922

facts.statement: Amanzia is a genus of turiasaurian sauropod dinosaur found in the Late Jurassic Reuchenette Formation in Moutier, Switzerland.
facts.quote: Amanzia (after Swiss geologist Amanz Gressly) is a genus of turiasaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic Reuchenette Formation in Moutier, Switzerland.

facts.statement: The fossils date to the Kimmeridgian stage, between 152.7 and 152 million years ago.
facts.quote: The Reuchenette Formation has been dated to the Kimmeridgian 152.7 to 152 million years ago.

facts.statement: The genus name Amanzia was established in 2020 by Schwarz et al. in honor of Amanz Gressly, the first person to discover dinosaur bones in Switzerland.
facts.quote: In 2020, Daniela Schwarz, Philip D. Mannion, Oliver Wings and Christian A. Meyer gave it the genus name Amanzia, after Swiss geologist Amanz Gressly, who was the first to discover dinosaur bones in Switzerland.

facts.statement: Amanzia is the first sauropod dinosaur to be named from remains found in Switzerland.
facts.quote: Amanzia is itself the first sauropod named from Swiss remains.

facts.statement: After cleaning and preparation in 2003, it was realized that the fossils were not closely related to Cetiosauriscus.
facts.quote: In 2003 by Antoine Heitz, it was realized not to be closely related to Cetiosauriscus.

facts.statement: In 2007, the rare preservation of fossilized cartilage in a limb joint was reported.
facts.quote: In 2007, the rare presence of fossilised cartilage in a limb joint was reported.

facts.statement: The fossil bones are not articulated, are strongly compressed, and were often damaged during removal from the rock.
facts.quote: The bones are not articulated, have generally been strongly compressed and had often been damaged when being forcefully removed from the rock.

facts.statement: While von Huene originally thought the material represented two or three individuals, a 2020 study concluded there were at least four individuals.
facts.quote: Von Huene had already concluded that the material represented two or three individuals; in 2020 this was increased to a minimum of four.

facts.statement: Among the four individuals, two are similar in size, one is 15% longer, and one is 20% shorter.
facts.quote: Of these, individuals "A" and "B" have about the same size, while an individual "C" is 15% longer and an individual "D" 20% shorter.

facts.statement: In 2020, seventy-five additional sauropod specimens from the same site were referred to the species Amanzia greppini.
facts.quote: Seventy-five additional sauropod specimens in the collection of the museum, from the same site as the syntypes, were in 2020 referred to the species.

facts.statement: Amanzia is classified within the family Turiasauria.
The dinosaur lived during the Late Jurassic, approximately 155 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 155 millones de años, en el Kimmeridgiense, en lo que hoy es Europa.

facts.statement: The time range for Amanzia is the Kimmeridgian, from 154.8 to 152.21 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Kimmeridgian (154.8 to 152.21 million years ago)
